_about: Public-domain Peter Thacher (1752-1802), minister of Malden and then of the Brattle Street Church, Boston, for the Word Hoard: his Watertown oration on the Boston Massacre (1776), a reply to the strictures of J. S. (1784), and his Boston sermons of 1798-1799. Texts are from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 109 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

pthacher-oration-1776: An oration delivered at Watertown, March 5, 1776. : To commemorate the bloody massacre at Boston: perpetrated March 5, 1770 (Watertown [Mass.] : Printed and sold by Benjamin Edes, on the bridge, 1776)
pthacher-reply-js: A reply to the strictures of Mr. J. S. a layman, upon the pamphlet entitled Observations upon the present state upon the present state of the clergy in New-England, &c. By Peter Thacher, A.M. author of said pamphlet.  1784 (catalogued 1784)
pthacher-brattle-1798: A sermon preached to the society in Brattle-street, Boston, March 25th, 1798 : and occasioned by the death of Madam Rebecca Gill, consort of his Honor Moses Gill, Esq., lieutenant-governor of the commonwealth of Massachusetts, who died March 19th, 1798, ætat. 70 (Boston : Printed by Rhoades and Laughton ..., 1798)
pthacher-first-church-1798: A sermon, delivered at the First Church in Boston, April 6, 1798,  1798 (catalogued 1798)
pthacher-gill-1799: A sermon preached June 12, 1799, before His Honor Moses Gill, esquire, lieutenant governor and commander in chief (Boston: Printed by Young & Minns, Printers to the Government of Massachusetts, 1799)
pthacher-brattle-1799: A sermon preached to the Church and Society in Brattle-Street, Boston, Dec. 29, 1799 : and occasioned by the completion of a century from its first establishment (Boston : Printed by Young & Minns ..., 1800)

_excluded.pthacher-others: The 1696 Saints' Victory and the 1730 Man's Frailty are by earlier Peter Thachers of Milton and Middleborough; the court reports are by Judge Peter O. Thacher
